title: Introduce credential synthesis layer and stream stabilizers across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs
author: Marina K. Ortiz
release_notes:
- Add CredentialSynthesis factory to unify delegated auth modes across SDKs
- Stabilize streaming backpressure by introducing a lightweight StreamStabilizer hook
- Patch several platform-specific streaming regressions and bump SDK versions (py 2.1.0, ts 1.8.0, go v1.5.2)
description:
Context and motivation: engineering teams have repeatedly asked for a single, predictable way to compose credential strategies (delegated tokens, short-lived leases, KMS-backed signatures) without duplicating logic across SDKs, and for a minimal cross-language surface to reduce streaming flakiness in long-lived connections. This PR introduces two complementary concepts: a CredentialSynthesis factory (polyglot, test-first) and a StreamStabilizer hook that lets SDKs provide deterministic backpressure hints and heartbeat glue.

What this PR does (summary): adds CredentialSynthesis implementations and adapters in python/typescript/go; normalizes SDK ergonomics so the same high-level calls create equivalent session metadata and refresh behavior; adds StreamStabilizer to each SDK which provides: (1) periodic implicit heartbeats when idle, (2) optional chunk coalescing hints for low-latency workloads, and (3) a lightweight flow-control callback for host applications to tune memory vs latency.

Checklist: [x] design doc (ENG-1349) linked and reviewed by infra; [x] unit + integration tests across three SDKs; [x] compatibility shims for existing clients; [x] migration notes and release entries; [ ] docs site walkthrough (follow-up PR).

Commits (high level): commit 1: "sdk: introduce credential_synthesis core interfaces (py/ts/go)" — adds interfaces and tests; commit 2: "sdk: implement stream_stabilizer & default heuristics" — core logic and TS streaming consumer fixes; commit 3: "sdk: harmonize examples + bump versions" — updates examples and bumps package versions.

Files touched (high level): python/src/redwood/auth/credential_synthesis.py, python/src/redwood/stream/stabilizer.py, typescript/src/cred/credentialSynthesis.ts, typescript/src/stream/stabilizer.ts, go/cred/synthesis.go, go/stream/stabilizer.go, examples/* (three example apps), test/integration/* (cross-sdk session scenarios), packaging/version bumps for py/ts/go. Small illustrative snippet included in the python adapter that shows the ergonomic factory use: "client = RedwoodClient(creds=CredentialSynthesis.from_env('lease'))".

Review conversation (abridged timeline):
- Evan Park (review): "Overall API looks good; my main concern is that the TS default coalescing heuristic might add latency for small-token workloads. Can we make coalescing opt-in with a safe default?"
- Marina (author): "Ack; made coalescing opt-in and added a runtime flag `coalesceWrites` default false for 1.8.0. Added unit tests to assert no additional latency for single-token responses."
- Lena Hoff (review): "Python changes look tight; one nit — prefer explicit async context manager for stabilizer lifecycle to avoid orphaned heartbeats in some serverless patterns."
- Marina: "Added Stabilizer.as_async_context() and updated examples; added integration test simulating serverless cold starts."
- Harold Tu (review): "Go has a race in the stabilizer stop path when client.Close() races with a heartbeat; suggest a WaitGroup or channel handshake."
- Marina: "Fixed with a channel-based shutdown handshake, added a unit test that forces concurrent Close and EmitHeartbeat. CI initially caught a flaky TS test that surfaced because our stream consumer test assumed coalescing; after toggling the default to off I re-ran the TS pipeline and everything passed."

CI summary: initial run: python unit/integration pass, go unit pass, typescript streaming integration flaky (1 failure - coalescing timing). After change (coalescing off by default) and re-run: all checks passed. End-to-end smoke in staging passed with a 48-hour soak.

Migration notes and consumer guidance: prefer CredentialSynthesis factory for new clients; legacy credential constructors still supported via `CredentialSynthesis.legacy_adapter()`; for streaming users: if your workload emits very small tokens at high frequency, do not enable coalesceWrites; for bursty long-lived streams consider enabling `stabilizer.heartbeat_interval_ms` tuning. Examples in repo/examples/describe-migration.md show direct substitutions.

Testing and validation: added cross-SDK integration harness that runs a 30-second chat loop across py/ts/go clients using a shared local test server; verified that refresh jitter and token swap scenarios cause zero dropped messages in 1000-run sampling.

Release and merging: bump python to 2.1.0, typescript to 1.8.0, go to v1.5.2. Changelog entries prepared and merged to main. Merged via squash after approvals.

If problems arise: revert is a single commit (revert: feature/cred-synthesis-stream-stabilizer) that will disable coalescing and remove stabilizer heartbeats quickly.

Notes: this change was intentionally conservative about defaults to avoid surprising latency regressions in low-latency clients; it's opt-in for the few heuristics that carry risk. Follow-up work (ENG-1350) will land a docs walkthrough and a small observability hook so customers can see stabilizer heartbeats in telemetry.

notes_for_consumers: New CredentialSynthesis factory is backwards-compatible; replace direct credential constructors with CredentialSynthesis.from_env(...) for better refresh semantics. StreamStabilizer defaults are conservative (coalesceWrites disabled). See examples/* and docs/release-notes for migration snippets.
post_merge_actions: - publish python 2.1.0 wheel to internal pip mirror; - publish npm 1.8.0 to internal registry; - tag go v1.5.2 and push to artifact store; - follow-up docs PR (ENG-1350) to add walkthrough
risk_assessment: Low-medium: default behavior is backwards compatible. Opt-in heuristics may change latency if enabled; tests and a 48-hour soak were performed in staging.
qa_summary: Unit tests added for all three SDKs; integration harness runs cross-lang session scenarios; flakiness previously observed in TS streaming was mitigated by making coalescing opt-in. QA signed off after 48h soak.
